mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate rate cuts.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the pre-inflation surprise period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) by more than 20,000 in a month is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >20,000 in a month
failure_condition: Across 5 consecutive months of strong employment growth, cumulative 60-day forward returns are not significantly above the mean of weak-growth periods (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in both HOUST (household consumption) and GDPC1 (GDP demand) by at least 2% and 1%, respectively, predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return through higher corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST up >=2% AND GDPC1 up >=1% in the same month
failure_condition: In 100 such coordinated demand months, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically higher than in non-coordinated months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% followed within 10 days by a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return reflects expectations of supply-side shocks easing production constraints.
failure_condition: During 5 such episodes, 20-day forward returns remain negative or flat (median return <= 0).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 shows a negative 20-day forward return as higher rates compress discounting of future earnings.
failure_condition: Over 30 such months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during stable rate periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in UNRATE (unemployment) below 4.5% predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market tightness supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: During 10 such tightness periods, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than average (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in RSAFS (retail sales) and HOUST (consumer spending) by at least 3% each are associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via stronger consumer confidence and earnings momentum.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS up >=3% AND HOUST up >=3% in the same month
regime_hint: strong retail and consumer demand expansion
failure_condition: In 50 such months, the 20-day forward return mean is not higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to post-crisis supply resilience (indicated by INDPRO rising by >4% in two consecutive months) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates sustained production stability.
failure_condition: During 10 such supply-resilient periods, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during pre-crisis volatility (p > 0.05).
